datasets: public retrieval datasets (ELI5, HotpotQA, FEVER, MIRACL, MS-MARCO, NQ, NLI, SQuAD, TriviaQA, Quora Duplicate Questions, Mr-TyDi, DuReader)
outputs: synthetic (query, positive, negative) samples for contrastive learning

changes_made.explanation: This paper focuses on text embedding models for retrieval and similarity tasks, not natural language generation. The synthesized data is used for training embedding models, not evaluating NLG outputs. Therefore, it does not address NLG tasks despite using LLMs for data synthesis.

The paper evaluates text embedding quality using MTEB benchmark scores and cosine similarity, but these metrics evaluate embedding quality for retrieval/similarity tasks, not generated text outputs. No NLG evaluation metrics are used.
No LLMs are used as judges to evaluate generated outputs. LLMs (GPT-4o, DeepSeek-V2) are used only for synthetic data generation, not for evaluation.
No human evaluation is conducted in this paper. The evaluation is entirely automatic using embedding benchmarks.

overall_notes: This paper addresses text embedding models for retrieval and semantic similarity tasks, not natural language generation (NLG). While it uses LLMs for synthetic data generation, the core focus is on improving embedding quality through better negative sampling and pooling methods. The extracted metadata incorrectly suggested NLG involvement, but careful reading shows this is an embedding/retrieval paper, not an NLG evaluation paper.
